newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks lower at open as profits taken.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks lower at open as profits taken.

text.p: The Australian share market slipped lower at the opening on Friday as modest selling pared the strong gains seen in recent days.
Turnover was inflated by the exercise of options after Thursday's expiry, with about A$700 million (US$555 million) of trade through the market pre-opening.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index lost 4.8 points to 2268.6.
Brokers said activity was slight with most stocks moving only several cents either way.
"There is not a great deal happening with most stocks only a few up or down and the volume is to do with options," said dealer Brett O'Donovan of brokerage Lance Jones.
O'Donovan noted that the September SPI futures contract closes out on Monday, saying jostling for position as the contract wound down may well dictate the finish for the day.
"Futures are off a little but they are still at a premium and hopefully that will hold until Monday," O'Donovan said.
Orbital Engine shares jumped early, albeit on very thin trade, after the company announced a deal to supply the Indonesian national car project with its combustion process engine.
Takeover target Discovery Petroleum also attracted attention after about 10 percent of its shares were crossed through broker James Capel at a price of A$0.75 per share.
The company is under a takeoffer from British oil group Premier Oil at A$0.70 per share.
Falls outnumbered rises by ratio of about five to two, while about 42 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
